```{python}
#| output: false
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "scripts")

studies = load("studies.csv")
```

## Row {height=50%}

```{python}
#| title: Studies by anchoring context
count_bar(anchoring["anchoring_context_label"], color="#41ab5d")
```

```{python}
#| title: Perception support
support = (studies["perception_support"]
           .map({True: "With perception cues", False: "No perception cues"})
           .fillna("No perception cues")
           .value_counts())
pct = support / support.sum() * 100
# counts and shares go into the category labels: plotly.js bar text labels
# render unreliably inside dashboard cards, axis labels always render
labels = [
    f"{name}<br>{v} ({p:.0f}%)"
    for name, v, p in zip(support.index, support.values, pct)
]
fig = px.bar(x=support.values, y=labels, orientation="h")
fig.update_traces(
    marker_color=COLOR_SEQ[: len(support)],
    hovertemplate="%{x} studies<extra></extra>",
)
fig.update_layout(
    xaxis_title="Number of studies",
    yaxis_title=None,
    margin=dict(l=10, r=10, t=10, b=10),
)
fig
```

```{python}
#| title: "Perception cues used (studies with perception support)"
# fold rarely used cues (fewer than 3 studies) into a single bucket
cue_labels = cues["perception_cues_label"]
counts = cue_labels.value_counts()
rare = counts[counts < 3].index
count_bar(cue_labels.replace(dict.fromkeys(rare, "Other pictorial")),
          color="#807dba")
```
